findings.title: A report table whose total includes a restricted benefit's value omits that benefit's row but carries no 'Includes restricted records' label, so the total does not reconcile and the hidden value can be read off it unlabelled
findings.reproduction: Candidate 832e5c82 (source d7b21bad3), disposable clone, PostgreSQL 16.15. Probe apps/api/test/integration/zz-domain/dom-r5-sensitive-escalation.test.ts, part (4) (copy: docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/domain/round-5/probes/dom-r5-sensitive-escalation.test.ts.txt). Run: QA_PG_PORT=30002 MTH_PORT_POOL=30003-30009 tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project integration apps/api/test/integration/zz-domain/. SYNTHETIC setup: seedClosureWorld; B01 = validatedBenefit (a Finance-validated measurement, 250000 SAR revenue_uplift; synthetic test data, not a real Finance decision); B02 = pendingBenefit, same class; the TO marks B01 sensitive. Then GET .../reports/registers/live?parameters={"register":"benefits"} and GET .../benefit-totals as TL (not admitted) and as TO (admitted). UI: e2e/zz-domain/dom-r5-screens.spec.ts part B on apps/web/e2e/support/with-stack.sh, where TL opens a benefits register snapshot generated by the TO and the benefits register page, en and ar.
findings.expected: D-195 Q3 (decided by the user) and ADR-0051 §2 'Totals and rollups': an aggregate that includes a sensitive record's value is computed identically for every reader. 'When a reader is not admitted to at least one sensitive record whose value the aggregate includes, the response carries includesRestrictedRecords: true and the screen shows the label "Includes restricted records" / "يشمل سجلات مقيدة". The record and its individual value are never shown.' BE-Z5 now omits the restricted row from report documents for such a reader. The table's totals still include its value, so the report response and the snapshot screen should carry that label, as GET /benefit-totals and the benefits page do.
findings.actual: For TL, the live report's table totals_sar_revenue_uplift has one row (B02: 0.0000 / 0.0000 / 0.0000) and totals realized_validated = 250000, realized_sustained = 0 and pending = 0. The row of B01 is omitted, but its value is kept in the total. The document has no restricted marker anywhere: the content schema (packages/shared/src/schemas/report.ts, strict) has no member for it, and the probe's /restricted/i scan of the response is false. For the same TL, GET /benefit-totals returns includesRestrictedRecords = true, and the benefits page shows 'Includes restricted records' (screenshots dom-r5-f280-tl-benefits.png, en and ar). The TL's view of the TO's snapshot shows the totals table with no label (dom-r5-f280-tl-register-snapshot.png, en and ar). The TO sees both rows and the same total. So the reader sees a total that does not equal the sum of the rows shown, with nothing to say why. When the restricted benefit is the only hidden member, the total minus the visible rows is exactly its individual value, and that is not labelled as restricted. BE-Z5's handback §6 recorded the missing member as an 'optional need' for the architect and orchestrator, and D-214 did not decide it. The same applies, by code reading, to every report assembler with totals or metrics over a sensitive record (documentForReader filters rows and leaves totals unchanged).

history.note: Raised in DG6 round 5 by domain-reviewer, judging BE-Z5's residual 'report totals kept as truthful verdicts' (D-214). Keeping the total is correct under D-195 Q3. The missing label is the defect. Medium (D-192: repair before the gate). It is not mandatory: the aggregate is the one the user decided every reader sees, but the label the user decided is missing. Suggested repair, for the architect and orchestrator: an additive optional includesRestrictedRecords on the report document or on the table section and metric (the ADR-0051 §2 pattern), set by documentForReader whenever it omits a row or source whose value a total or metric includes; the report and snapshot screens render RestrictedRecordsLabel next to those totals (en/ar); stored content and contentSha256 unchanged (read-time flag); exports refused as today; a negative test (TL, AUD) and a positive one (TO: false).

findings.title: ADR-0053 still states a strict If-Match rule for acknowledge and resolve; the shipped rule that accepts a version behind only by system recurrences (T-DG6-BE-Z6) is not recorded in the ADR
findings.reproduction: Read docs/architecture/adr/ADR-0053-p6-operations-service-identities-exceptions-logs-heartbeat.md §2 (line 150: 'Every mutation: authorization re-checked at commit, validation, If-Match (409/428)…'; line 97: '409 version conflict … the ADR-0007 §5b shared problems'), then apps/api/src/modules/operations/exceptions.ts rebaseOverSystemOccurrences and the T-DG6-BE-Z6 handback §7 ('For the architect (ADR-0053 §2 amendment): please record the If-Match rule … with an "as shipped" note'). git log on ADR-0053 shows no change after T-DG6-ARCH-14.
findings.expected: A shipped deviation from the shared optimistic-concurrency rule (ADR-0003/ADR-0007 §5b: an If-Match that is not the current version is 409) is recorded as a dated amendment of the ADR that owns it, as the DG6 ADRs do for every other as-shipped rule.
findings.actual: The behaviour is sound (judged in DOM-R5-05) and is described only in the two OpenAPI operation summaries and the BE-Z6 handback. ADR-0053 §2 still reads as a strict If-Match rule, including no `based_on_version` audit field. Documentation drift only: no behavioural effect.

history.note: Raised in DG6 round 5 by domain-reviewer, judging BE-Z6 (D-214). Low, documentation only, not blocking. Suggested repair: a dated ADR-0053 §2 amendment recording rebaseOverSystemOccurrences (accepted only when every intervening history event is `recurred` with no user; anything else 409), the `based_on_version` audit field, and the resolve-after-recurrence consequence (the folded occurrence stays counted on the resolved row; the next failure opens a new exception).
